newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Major Dutch gas storage facility begins operation.
newsitem.headline: Major Dutch gas storage facility begins operation.

text.p: A cornerstone of the Dutch gas industry's efforts to meet peak winter demand, the Grypskerk storage facility, came into operation at the start of this year, Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM) said on Friday.
The Grypskerk gas field, developed at a cost of a billion guilders, is destined to be a storage facility with a capacity of 80 million cubic metres to meet peak winter demand.
"We are now producing this field through the new facility. In summer, we will start injecting gas for the first time," said a NAM spokesman.
As a new gas field, Grypskerk must first produce before gas can be stored.
Another storage facility, Langelo, on the existing Norg field, is expected to be completed by the end of the year, ready for gas injection in the summer of 1998.
A smaller site at Alkmaar, to meet daily peaks in demand, is already in operation.

The storage facilities are necessary because of the reduced pressure of the Netherlands' main Groningen field. Work on compressing and upgrading 29 installations at the field is due to begin this year. The first upgraded installation is due to start in the winter of 1998/1999, but will not be completed until around 2010.
NAM is jointly owned by Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.
